pixel: One tiny square of a picture. To a computer it is just a number saying how bright (or how inky) that square is.
MNIST: A famous collection of 70,000 handwritten digits, each 28 × 28 pixels, used to test image-reading networks since the 1990s.
flatten: To unroll a grid of numbers into one long list, row after row, so it can be fed to a layer of neurons.
fully connected: A layer where every neuron is wired to every input. It treats the inputs as a plain list and has no idea which ones are neighbors.
preprocessing: Tidying raw data into the shape a model expects before the model sees it, the same way for training and for real use.
center of mass: The balance point of a shape: the spot where it would balance on a fingertip.
dead neuron: A ReLU neuron that outputs 0 for every input. No blame flows back through it, so it never learns again.
